rationale: A systematic review with a harmonised uptake outcome answers the executive's question better than any local study could in time. Controlled studies of prompts (c1) and of training with feedback (c2) exist, and the definitions problem (c4) is manageable if every study is coded against a core definition. Pooling is planned only where three or more studies share a definition and design; otherwise a structured synthesis without meta-analysis is reported.
alternatives: Rapid review (refused: the purchase decision can wait for a full review by mid-2027, and definitions need careful coding)
Local pilot of the prompt in one clinic (refused as the first step: it would not tell the executive how the prompt compares with training)
Umbrella review (refused: too few existing reviews on uptake strategies)
whyNotMoreComplex: An individual participant data review would be far beyond two part-time reviewers and is not needed for a strategy comparison.

decision.statement: Conduct a systematic review of strategies to increase completed and clinician-reviewed symptom measures in outpatient depression care, coding every study against a core uptake definition, with meta-analysis only where at least three studies share a definition and design.
decision.question: Should the service commission a systematic review before choosing between an electronic prompt and clinician training with feedback?

criteria.text: Controlled studies of both candidate strategies exist.
Uptake definitions can be harmonised against a core definition.
A recent review already compares these strategies on a harmonised uptake outcome.

gates.requirement: Second reviewer released from clinical duties for about 60 hours of dual screening and extraction
Librarian support to build and run the search
gates.evidence: Service librarian agreement of 2026-09-10 to build and run the search in November 2026, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Local pilot of the prompt in one clinic
decision.note: Rests on claims c1, c2 and c4; dual screening cannot start until the second reviewer is released.

summary: Systematic review recommended; the second-reviewer gate is unknown.
